column1: # The calibration contract for autospec's live-region gate, measured against
# skills/autospec-shared/scripts/ui-liveregion-evidence.mjs.
# This tier differs from the lint corpus in EXPECTED.tsv: it cannot read files, it has to
# drive the app. Every route below exposes window.__autospec.setState, and the gate calls
# it and watches what a screen reader would have been told. Run ./check-liveregions.sh.
# A rule id of "-" means no finding is expected for that route.
# route
# The reference implementation. Three states, three clean announcements — including a
# loading state that correctly stays aria-busy, declared in .autospec/ui-test-hooks.json so
# the gate does not read it as a flag left stuck.
/states.html[loading]
/states.html[error]
/states.html[success]
# The corpus. One route per rule, so a rule that stops firing is visible as one row.
/fixtures/live-regions/inserted-with-content.html[success]
/fixtures/live-regions/silent-update.html[success]
/fixtures/live-regions/hidden-region.html[success]
/fixtures/live-regions/stuck-busy.html[success]
/fixtures/live-regions/shouted-status.html[success]
/fixtures/live-regions/no-hook.html[success]
/fixtures/live-regions/inert-hook.html[success]
# TEST_HOOK_FAILED needs no fixture of its own: states.html already throws on a state name
# it does not know, so a manifest carrying a typo produces it exactly as a real one would.
/states.html[sucess]
# Two false-positive guards are carried inside fixtures rather than as rows of their own,
# because the assertion is an absence:
#   hidden-region.html   also fills an .sr-only region, which is hidden the correct way and
#                        stays in the accessibility tree. Exactly one HIDDEN row above, not
#                        two, is what proves the gate leaves it alone.
#   states.html[loading] leaves aria-busy set on purpose. A clean row is what proves the
#                        manifest's "busy": true declaration is honoured.
